AUTHOR: Wang, GA; Hwang, JN; Williams, K; Cutter, G
TITLE: Closed-Loop Tracking-by-Detection for ROV-Based Multiple Fish Tracking
VENUE: 2016 ICPR 2ND WORKSHOP ON COMPUTER VISION FOR ANALYSIS OF UNDERWATER IMAGERY (CVAUI 2016)
REGION: NR (NOAA Alaska Fisheries Science Center ROV data)
D2: DPM trained on 1,067 images; tested on 2 video sequences (>4,000 frames, 134 tracklets); tracklet classifier 10-fold CV
D_EV: Sec IV.A: 'The DPM detector is trained on 1,067 images extracted from underwater video sequences' - no statement whether test videos were disjoint
R_EV: Sec IV.A: 'The proposed work is tested on two long underwater video sequences with over 4,000 frames and a total of 134 tracklets.'
C_EV: Sec IV.A: 'The detection threshold is set to be -0.5'; Table I confusion matrix of fish/non-fish tracklets vs ground truth (5 non-fish classified as fish)
E_EV: Table II Counting Error: 'Clip1 (15 fish) ... Clip2 (9 fish) ... Closed-Loop with DPM and Motion Scores 1 1'
ARCH: DPM detector + epipolar motion score + naive Bayes tracklet classifier + multiple kernel tracking
NOTE: Split unit between detector training images and the two test videos not stated (D1=NR). Tracklet classifier evaluated by 10-fold CV over tracklets of the test videos. C5 credited because tracklet-level false positives are counted against ground-truth labels (Table I) and removed by the classifier; verifier may judge this not C5 (then C_ALL=N; threshold -0.5 rationale only verbal). Counts compared with true fish numbers per clip (human annotation of same footage).
